issues.description: Column / join key inconsistency: the solution's WHERE clause uses Freizeitpark.id as the municipality foreign key (WHERE Gemeinde.schluessel = Freizeitpark.id), but the problem statement and the intended data model imply that Freizeitpark should reference its Gemeinde via a foreign-key column (e.g., Freizeitpark.gemeindeschluessel). The template does not provide a join condition. This mismatch (solution uses Freizeitpark.id instead of Freizeitpark.gemeindeschluessel) will produce incorrect joins or confuse students about which column is the foreign key to connect Freizeitpark and Gemeinde.
issues.suggestedFix: Replace the join in the solution with the correct foreign-key column from Freizeitpark. For example change the WHERE clause to: WHERE Gemeinde.schluessel = Freizeitpark.gemeindeschluessel. Also update any accompanying explanation or template guidance to indicate that Freizeitpark.gemeindeschluessel is the FK referencing Gemeinde.schluessel.

issues.description: Concept: the foreign-key column that links a facility row to its Gemeinde (municipality). Problem statement (Aufgabe 02) asks for Freizeitpark rows joined to Gemeinde but does not name join columns. Template (template_repository/aufgabe02.sql) provides SELECT and FROM but no join condition (lines 1-2) so it does not establish which Freizeitpark column links to Gemeinde. Solution (solution_repository/aufgabe02.sql) uses Freizeitpark.id in the join condition (WHERE Gemeinde.schluessel = Freizeitpark.id, line 3). Other solution files and the schema use a consistent foreign-key identifier pattern: <Table>.gemeindeschluessel (e.g., Zoo.gemeindeschluessel, Schwimmbad.gemeindeschluessel). Using Freizeitpark.id for the same conceptual foreign-key relationship creates an identifier-naming inconsistency that can confuse students about which column to use for joins and how the schema is designed.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the foreign-key name consistent across artifacts: either change the solution to use Freizeitpark.gemeindeschluessel in the WHERE clause (WHERE Gemeinde.schluessel = Freizeitpark.gemeindeschluessel) and update the template to hint or include that column, or explicitly document in the problem statement/schema that Freizeitpark.id is the gemeindeschluessel. Align template and solution so students can unambiguously map the join relationship.
